steps: The de Broglie wavelength of an electron is related to its kinetic energy K by λ = h / √(2mK).
A convenient approximation for an electron is λ (in Å) ≈ √(150 / K (in eV)).
The given wavelength is 0.3 nm, which is equal to 3 Å.
Substituting λ = 3 Å into the formula gives 3 = √(150 / K).
Squaring both sides yields 9 = 150 / K, so K = 150 / 9 = 16.67 eV.
This value is closest to 16.8 eV, which matches option (B).
